author: Andrew Gamble
title: Mauricio Pochettino reaction to Folarin Balogun red card says it all - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Gamble ,
58 minutes ago USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino could not hide his disbelief as Folarin Balogun was shown a red card in the World Cup.
On Wednesday night in Seattle, the United States clinched a first knockout win since 2002 with a thrilling 2-0 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina. Balogun opened the scoring with a fine finish late in the first half to get his third of the World Cup , while Malik Tillman secured the USMNT ’s Round of 32 win with a stunning free kick.
However, one moment will stick out and grab the headlines. Between the two goals, Balogun was shown a straight red card for violent conduct as he was deemed to have raked his studs down the calf of Bosnia defender Tarik Muharemovic.

• 'Disgraceful' Folarin Balogun red card at World Cup sends internet into meltdown
The incident occurred in the 64th minute, and Balogun appeared stunned as the weight of the impending decision dawned on him. VAR instructed Brazilian referee Raphael Claus to go to the monitor and, moments later, showed the striker a red card.
As Claus described the incident as a “serious foul” and showed him a red card, Pochettino stood on the sidelines with his arms spread wide in disbelief. The Argentinian then shook his fists in the air and, with a smirk on his face, approached the fourth official to try and understand the thought behind the call.
Balogun trudged slowly to the dressing room, and the U.S. was forced to play the rest of the match with 10 men. The decision meant he became the fifth American to receive a red card in the World Cup after Eric Wynalda against Czechoslovakia in 1990, Fernando Clavijo against Brazil in 1994, and Pablo Mastroeni and Eddie Pope against Italy in 2006.
Balogun is also the first player to score and be sent off in a World Cup knockout game since France great Zinedine Zidane was infamously shown a red card for a head-butt in the 2006 World Cup final.

Unfortunately, FIFA’s Disciplinary Committee has the power to extend Folarin Balogun’s suspension beyond the Round of 16 tie against Belgium, but the body cannot overturn or reduce a ban. This means Pochettino must find another option in attack for Monday’s big game in Seattle.
After the game, Pochettino addressed Balogun's sending off and said: “For me, it’s never a red card. I looked at it on TV, there never was intention, and to step on the player was a normal action in football that happened by accident. It was never intentional. For me, this was never intentional.”
USMNT superstar Christian Pulisic spoke out, saying he “didn’t see” the red card incident but was proud of his team’s resilience. After the game, he said: “We had to dig deep for that one. Obviously, I felt like we put on such a good performance and didn’t deserve the red card. I didn’t see it, but it’s unfortunate.
“For us to dig in deep like that, and just to get another goal and defend the way we did, it took a real team effort. We’re proud of that.”
Tillman, who scored a sensational second, added: “I think this shows our character. We’ve said it before a lot of times, we’re always there for each other, no matter what. I think today showed that.”
The USMNT will take on Belgium, who clinched a 3-2 win over Senegal, in Seattle on Monday, July 6.
